A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disk around CoKu Tau is truncated, and the inner hole has a size of about 10 AU.
we have modeled the spectrum of CoKU Tau/4 as arising from the wall of a disk with a cleared inner zone of radius 10 AU and a dusty wall of height 2 AU, with no evidence for crystalline silicates.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the inner disk wall can produce a spectrum similar to that of a disk with a large inner hole.
the mid-infrared spectra of young stars are sensitive to the physical conditions in the inner disk wall.
the mid-infrared spectra of disks can be used to probe the physical structure of the disk, and in particular the presence of an inner hole, which may be a signpost of the formation of planets.
